title: Data on Sanctioned Individuals Operating Tax-exempt Family Offices Locally
what_it_is: Data on Sanctioned Individuals Operating Tax-exempt Family Offices Locally

sections.label: Chen Zhi probes and SFO rejections
sections.summary: Police probed Chen Zhi before US indictment; MAS found two SFO funds linked to sanctioned individuals, and about 3% of 1,300 applications were rejected.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: Prior to the indictment of Chen Zhi by the United States (US), our Police had been conducting probes into Chen Zhi and his associates.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: Thus far, the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) has identified two Single Family Offices (SFO) funds granted tax incentives that are linked to the sanctioned individuals.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: Based on available data over the past three years, about 3% out of 1,300 applications were rejected.

sections.label: New SFO notification requirements
sections.summary: All Singapore SFOs must maintain bank accounts, notify MAS when starting operations, and submit annual returns to MAS.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: In addition to now requiring all SFOs based in Singapore, whether they are receiving tax incentives or not, to maintain bank accounts, SFOs will need to notify MAS upon the commencement of their operations and submit annual returns to MAS.

sections.label: Local bank wealth management employment
sections.summary: As at end 2024, banks' wealth management and private banking functions employed more than 13,000 locals.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: As at end 2024, the wealth management and private banking functions in banks employed more than 13,000 locals.

sections.label: Questions on MAS reviews and rescreening
sections.summary: Supplementary questions ask whether MAS reviewed DW Capital Holdings, whether illicit money has penetrated Singapore, and whether existing 13O and 13U holders will be rescreened.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Three supplementary questions for the Minister, given that Prince Group's scam operations were publicly documented by English language investigative media as early as February 2024 and even earlier in July 2022 in Chinese court notices, did MAS conduct any mid-term reviews of DW Capital Holdings between 2018 and the US action in October 2025?

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I think there are a lot of flies in the house.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: So, as more cases of criminality associated with family offices that have been set up in Singapore have come to light, will the Government start to work on the assumption that illicit money generated by scams and other cross-border crime has already penetrated Singapore?

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: And therefore, will the Government mandate enhanced due diligence on existing client relationships across all regulated financial sectors, not just new client onboarding?

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Further to my previous question, will MAS require all existing 13O and 13U tax incentive holders, and not just new applicants, undergo mandatory rescreening?

sections.label: Risk-proportionate financial centre approach
sections.summary: The speaker says a zero-risk approach is impractical and urges a risk-proportionate, calibrated approach to maintain standards and competitiveness.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: So, he could have just said that and not add on all the other additional comments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: So, if we agree with that, that it is not practical to adopt a zero-risk approach, then I think we can take a look at what are some of the moves that we can make to maintain high standards on one hand, that is important, we want to remain a trusted financial centre; and at the same time, remain efficient and competitive.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: If Mr Tiong believes that being inefficient, being overly cumbersome, adopting a zero-risk approach, being overly risk adverse, is the right way to go, I think if we follow his advice, our financial hub status is at risk.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: We need to take a risk-proportionate, calibrated approach, just like all other major international financial centres – maintain high standards, deter bad actors, take action against them when we discover wrongdoings.

sections.label: Singapore flies and SFO convictions
sections.summary: The speaker says Singapore does not have many flies and that SFOs convicted of money laundering represent less than 1%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: I do not know which "house" Mr Tiong is referring to, but as far as we are aware, the house of Singapore, we do not have many flies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: I mentioned earlier that the SFOs that are involved in money laundering and are convicted for money laundering, represent less than 1%.

sections.label: Bank STRs and family office registration
sections.summary: Banks file suspicious transaction reports and rules are being reviewed, while family office registration may be shortened from 12 months to three months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: I mentioned earlier that the banks do file STRs, and we are also in the process of reviewing what our rules should be, so that we are able to maintain high standards, we are able to deter bad actors from wanting to come to Singapore and importantly, maintain our competitiveness as a financial centre.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: It was reported in July that the Minister in his capacity in the MAS had announced that there was an intention to shorten the process of registration for family offices, I think, from 12 months to three months, to make it faster for these offices to open bank accounts and to claim their tax incentives.

sections.label: Streamlining processes and anti-money laundering checks
sections.summary: Processes are streamlined through technology and information sharing to block suspicious cases without changing anti-money laundering checks on applicants.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: And it is also to look at how we can streamline the processes so that, through the use of technology, through the use of information sharing, we make it more efficient, so that we do not deter the genuine cases, but we block out and we do not admit the ones that are suspicious and have problems that will affect our high standards and reputation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: It is a fine calibration, but I want to assure Ms Lim that what we recently announced is meant to simplify the requirements and improve operational efficiency.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: It does not change the anti-money laundering checks that we submit the applicants to.

sections.label: Competitive financial and wealth management industry
sections.summary: The financial services and wealth management industries should remain competitive, and the sector supports at least 13,000 local jobs.

sentences.text: We do want our financial services industry to remain competitive, our wealth management industry to remain competitive.
I mentioned in my main reply that this sector supports at least 13,000 local jobs and may grow further.

sections.label: Prince Holdings case action
sections.summary: Authorities have taken action in the Prince Holdings case in recent weeks, not only in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: If you look at what is happening to the Prince Holdings case, it is not just in Singapore, where the authorities have taken action in recent weeks.

sections.label: SFO checks and MAS tax exemption checks
sections.summary: Checks are done at two levels: banks conduct due diligence before opening accounts, and MAS checks tax exemption applicants.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: And if not, could I request that the Government consider requiring the SFO to do so because, after all, it is the first gatekeeper in any of this relationship with a new family office?

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: So, this is something which we will be sharing more details on the date of implementation and also, to look at what are the changes to the legislation that we will need.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: The point that Mr Tan mentioned earlier about doing the checks, we do that.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: And we do that at two levels, so the banks will, on their own, do some of these checks with the clients before they allow them to open accounts, and that is part of their due diligence checks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: And for MAS, we will do another check if they are applying for tax exemption.
